candidate.answerReason: The projection rectangle gives \(PQ=ON\), where \(O\) is the diagonal intersection. The minimum is the altitude to the hypotenuse of an 8-15-17 right triangle, namely \(120/17\). Its foot lies inside \(AB\), and the closest listed value is 7, agreeing with C.

methods.label: Replace the moving segment by a distance
methods.explanation:
Let \(O\) be the intersection of the rhombus's diagonals. A rhombus's diagonals bisect each other at right angles, so
\[
OA=8,\qquad OB=15,
\]
and \(AOB\) is a right triangle. The Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
AB=\sqrt{8^2+15^2}=17.
\]

The useful observation is that \(PQ\) equals \(ON\). For \(N\) in the interior of \(AB\), the quadrilateral \(OPNQ\) has right angles at \(O,P,Q\), so it is a rectangle. Its diagonals \(PQ\) and \(ON\) are equal. At the endpoints this equality still holds directly: when \(N=A\), the feet are \(P=A,Q=O\); when \(N=B\), they are \(P=O,Q=B\).

Thus we need the point of \(AB\) nearest to \(O\). Let \(H\) be the perpendicular foot from \(O\) to \(AB\). Both angles at \(A\) and \(B\) in the right triangle are acute, so \(H\) lies inside \(AB\). For every allowed \(N\), the Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
ON^2=OH^2+HN^2\ge OH^2,
\]
with equality exactly when \(N=H\). This proves that the minimum is attained and equals \(OH\).

Compute this altitude by expressing the area of \(AOB\) using two different bases:
\[
\frac12(17)(OH)=\frac12(8)(15).
\]
Hence
\[
\min PQ=OH=\frac{120}{17}.
\]
Since \(7<120/17<7.125\), the value lies between \(7\) and the midpoint of \(7\) and \(7.25\). Therefore the closest listed value is \(\boxed{7}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
